quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the right footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on things. Tuck in all laces so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: What does swerving a motorcycle require?

options.text: It should be done to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick maneuver that needs a lot of traction to do safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you usually do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can prevent drunk driving by arranging other transportation, involving them in other activities to slow their drinking, finding excuses to keep them from leaving before they're sober, and asking other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a cause of a wobble on your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to stop a wobble.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you on your left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far right as possible to help them.
Move to the shoulder to help them.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause them to merge back too soon. Center position is safest.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they may seem to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling slower than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Because of their small size, motorcycles can look like they are moving faster than they really are.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: They don't need to reach the footrests.
They should hold the motorcycle frame.

questions.explanation: A child should always sit right behind the operator. A child in front may not balance well and could block the operator's controls.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.
Either the left or right portion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you farthest from opening car doors, people stepping between cars, and cars pulling out.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: They never need to be replaced.
They develop scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
They should be made of breakable materials so they break in a crash.
They should not let any air pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They develop scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. They will scratch and become brittle as they age. Replace them regularly to stay protected and comfortable.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use brakes. Downshift instead.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. When is this strip safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this strip usually provides enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is often only two feet wide, so you can usually ride around it and still stay in the center lane.

questions.question: A dog is chasing your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, downshift and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you turn?
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what should a rider do?

options.text: Lean shoulders to match the turn angle.

questions.explanation: Before turning, reduce your speed by closing the throttle and applying both brakes if needed.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is how many times more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet?
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because you will be seen easily.
No, because drivers rarely check side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
No, because it is illegal to ride outside the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a vehicle, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time.
Either brake or swerve, but not both.
Only use the front brake, do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Perform braking and swerving separately. Do not do both at the same time, as this may cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Perform braking and swerving separately. Either brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both actions at the same time.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out your path.

questions.question: As weight transfers to the front of your bike while you are braking, you should:

options.text: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
Not worry. The weight transfer will not have an effect on your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
questions.explanation: While braking, gradually increase the pressure on the front brake lever as the bike's weight moves forward to the front tire.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These regulatory signs tell drivers what rules to follow on the road.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing the braking pressure of the front brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.
